components.name: MapLibre GL JS
components.desc: The open-source WebGL map renderer that draws the whole map: vector and raster layers, globe, 3D terrain, hillshade, labels.
components.detail: Downloaded with the Base map package (not part of the app files) and loaded on demand by `loadMapLib` (maps.js) from the cache 'pult-maps'. Version 5.24.0 (base/lib5) is used; 4.7.1 (base/lib) only if an older download lacks version 5. Pult hooks into it through custom protocols (pmtiles://, pultglyph://, maplibre-contour's), custom layers (sky bodies, three.js obelisk) and two small source patches.
components.netNote: needs the Base map package (downloaded once)

mem: est. 30-150 MB: parsed engine, tile caches, GeoJSON sources, style
cpu: tile parsing in its worker pool; style rebuilds on setting changes; per-frame layout
gpu: every map frame: all layers, globe, terrain

components.name: MapLibre 5.24
components.desc: The map engine in use: globe projection, 3D terrain, hillshade, color-relief, fill-extrusion and custom WebGL layers.
components.detail: Loaded from maps/base/lib5 (script + CSS) via a patched blob URL (see the patches). The map is created in `showMap1` with globe or Mercator projection, max pitch 85, zoom 0-16; a 'webglcontextlost' listener reports lost graphics memory on phones. Version 5 is required for color-relief (height colours) and the globe atmosphere.
components.netNote: from the Base map package

mem: est. 30-150 MB with tile caches and GeoJSON sources
cpu: worker-pool tile parsing; main-thread layout and placement per frame
gpu: renders every frame while the map moves; terrain and globe add cost

components.name: MapLibre 4.7 (fallback)
components.desc: The previous engine version, used only when a Base map downloaded before v295 lacks version 5.
components.detail: `engineDir` checks the cache for base/lib5/maplibre-gl.js and otherwise loads base/lib unpatched. Features that need version 5 (height colours, the sun-shading patch) are then missing; `engineMajor` lets the relief code tell.
components.netNote: from the Base map package

components.name: Pult's patches to MapLibre
components.desc: Small text replacements in the MapLibre 5 script so hillshading follows the real sun at every point, and the obelisk is lit by its own sun.
components.detail: `shadePatchedLib` (maprelief.js) fetches the script text, applies `SHADE_PATCH` (new uniforms u_lngrange, u_sun, u_sun2 and per-pixel sun azimuth and night fade in the hillshade shader, fed from self.__pultSun) and `OB_PATCH` (fill-extrusion light from self.__pultObLight), and loads the result from a blob URL. `enginePatch` applies each group whole or not at all: if a piece is not found exactly (another version), that group is skipped and the engine runs unchanged.

mem: a second copy of the ~1 MB script as a string and blob while loading
store: nothing stored (patched in memory at each start)
cpu: once per map start: string splits over 1 MB
gpu: a few extra shader instructions per hillshade pixel

components.name: Custom tile protocols
components.desc: Address schemes MapLibre calls back into for data: pmtiles:// (map packages), pultglyph:// (contour figures) and maplibre-contour's DEM and contour schemes.
components.detail: Registered with `maplibregl.addProtocol`: `pmInit` (maps.js) for PMTiles, `glyphInit` (maprelief.js) for the self-made glyphs, and `DemSource.setupMaplibre` for elevation and contour tiles. They let fully offline data and in-app generated data appear to the engine as ordinary tile URLs.

components.name: three.js
components.desc: The 3D library (r169) used to draw the porphyry obelisk as a lit, textured model inside the map.
components.detail: Imported lazily as an ES module (`threeLib` in mapsun.js) only when the obelisk is shown; if it cannot load, MapLibre's fill-extrusion blocks stand in. The service worker keeps lib/ in the cache 'pult-lib' across app updates.
components.netNote: fetched once from the app's site, then from the cache 'pult-lib'

mem: est. 3-8 MB: parsed module + one scene
cpu: parse once; scene update per frame while shown
gpu: one small mesh per map frame

components.name: Module loading
components.desc: Loads lib/three-0.169.0.module.min.js by dynamic import, once.
components.detail: `threeLib` memoises the import promise; failures are logged and return null so the map keeps the extrusion fallback. The service worker's lib/ rule serves the file cache-first from 'pult-lib' (the version is in the file name, so no revalidation is needed).
components.netNote: first use needs the network

components.name: Renderer in the map's GL context
components.desc: A three.js WebGLRenderer drawing into MapLibre's own canvas and WebGL context as a custom 3D layer.
components.detail: `obel3dLayer` (mapsun.js) creates the renderer with MapLibre's gl context (autoClear off), a camera fed from the map's projection matrix, MeshStandardMaterial with a 256 px procedural porphyry texture, and sun and sky lights. The depth buffer is shared, so hills and the globe hide the model.

gpu: a few hundred triangles with PBR shading per frame

components.name: maplibre-contour
components.desc: Library (Michael Barry, BSD-3) that turns elevation tiles into contour lines on the fly and serves elevation data to the app.
components.detail: Loaded as a classic script (`addScript('maplibre-contour.js')` in `reliefInit`) only when relief is available (online, or an area is saved). One `DemSource` for Mapterhorn is created per session with worker on, a cache of 24 tiles and a 30 s timeout.
components.netNote: works offline from saved relief areas

mem: est. ~25-40 MB: up to 24 decoded 512 px DEM tiles + contour tiles
cpu: in a worker: WebP decode + isoline tracing per tile

components.name: DEM source
components.desc: The library entry point: `mlcontour.DemSource`, which fetches and decodes elevation tiles and plugs itself into MapLibre.
components.detail: The whole bundled library (one minified UMD script defining the global `mlcontour`, with its worker code embedded as a blob) is this declaration. `setupMaplibre` registers its protocols; `getDemTile` returns decoded heights, which Pult uses for heights on tap and profiles of drawn lines (`profileOf`).
components.netNote: tiles from Mapterhorn or the saved-relief cache

cpu: request bookkeeping on the main thread

components.name: Contour worker
components.desc: A Web Worker that decodes the WebP tiles and traces the contour lines away from the page.
components.detail: Started from a blob URL built from the bundled worker code; decodes with createImageBitmap and OffscreenCanvas, then runs marching-squares isolines at the levels Pult asks for (spacing from `contSpacing`, units from the settings).

mem: decoded tiles in the worker (est. 1 MB per 512 px tile)

components.name: Contour vector tiles
components.desc: Contour lines delivered to MapLibre as vector tiles through `contourProtocolUrl`.
components.detail: maprelief.js builds the source 'contours' (layer 'contours', keys 'ele' and 'level', overzoom 1, multiplier for feet or metres); the numbers are labelled with the self-made glyphs from TinySDF.

components.name: pmtiles.js
components.desc: Library (Protomaps, 4.4.1) that reads tiles out of single-file PMTiles archives.
components.detail: Shipped in the Base map package (base/lib/pmtiles.js) and loaded after MapLibre when present; `pmInit` registers its `Protocol` as pmtiles://. Instead of HTTP range requests, Pult gives it a `CacheSource` that slices the whole archive blob kept in the cache 'pult-maps', so every PMTiles package works offline.
components.netNote: archives come from downloaded map packages

mem: archive directories + the blob handle per package (est. a few MB)
cpu: directory decompression and lookups per tile

components.name: pmtiles:// protocol
components.desc: Answers MapLibre's tile requests for pmtiles:// sources.
components.detail: `pmUrl` (maps.js) adds one `PMTiles` instance per downloaded archive and returns its pmtiles:// address for the style; the protocol finds the archive and returns the tile bytes.

components.name: Archive reader
components.desc: Reads the archive header and directories and locates each tile's byte range.
components.detail: Reads through `CacheSource.getBytes` (blob.slice of the cached file); directories are gzip-compressed and unpacked with DecompressionStream.

components.name: TinySDF
components.desc: Mapbox's small library (2.3.0, BSD-2) that draws letters as signed distance fields in a canvas; Pult uses it for the figures of contour numbers.
components.detail: Imported as a module by `pultGlyphs` (maprelief.js), it renders 15 characters (digits, comma, minus, point, space) in Source Sans 3 600 at 24 px, which Pult packs into a glyph protocol buffer for MapLibre. This avoids a glyph server and keeps contour labels offline in the app's own font.

components.name: Glyph drawing
components.desc: Draws one character into a canvas and converts its alpha into a distance field.
components.detail: The `TinySDF` class (module top level) uses one 2D canvas of font size + 4 × buffer (36 px here), draws the glyph, and maps alpha through the gamma-corrected `alphaTable` into inner and outer distance grids before running the transform.

components.name: Distance transform
components.desc: The Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher Euclidean distance transform behind the distance fields.
components.detail: `edt` runs `edt1d` over columns and then rows of the glyph area; `INF` (1e20) marks unset cells.

cpu: linear in pixels, once per glyph

components.name: Browser platform
components.desc: The web platform features the app depends on: WebGL, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, the service worker, compression streams, Web Workers and canvas.
components.detail: Pult has no server-side logic: storage, offline use, decompression and all graphics run on these browser APIs. Missing features are reported rather than worked around (e.g. no DecompressionStream → a message asking to update iPadOS).

store: the quota of the site's origin (usage shown in Instruments)

components.name: WebGL
components.desc: The GPU drawing API under the map: MapLibre's renderer and the three.js obelisk share one WebGL context.
components.detail: Custom layers ('skybodies' 2D, 'obel3d' 3D) draw into MapLibre's context. When the system takes the graphics memory back (common on phones), the 'webglcontextlost' event is turned into a readable error with a retry button.

mem: GPU buffers and textures mirrored in RAM (est.)

components.name: IndexedDB
components.desc: The browser database holding settings, texts, dictionaries, the library, places and the search index.
components.detail: Opened with `indexedDB.open` in core.js (settings and one database per dictionary), library.js, maps.js (places) and search.js. The app asks for persistent storage (`navigator.storage.persist`) at start and before downloads, and shows usage and free space from `navigator.storage.estimate`.

store: hundreds of MB with several dictionaries and texts

components.name: Cache Storage
components.desc: Named HTTP response caches: the app files, map packages, saved relief, libraries and download parts.
components.detail: Used both by the service worker and directly from the page (`caches.open` in maps.js, maprelief.js, dialogs.js). Responses are stored under their real addresses, so cached map files and Mapterhorn tiles can be requested as ordinary URLs.

store: map packages and saved relief: up to GBs

components.name: Service worker
components.desc: The background script that makes the app work offline and answers requests from the caches.
components.detail: Registered in app.js (`navigator.serviceWorker.register('sw.js')`, not on file://); it imports reliefsw.js and routes requests by path and host. Activation deletes old app caches but keeps 'pult-maps', 'pult-relief' and 'pult-lib'.

mem: a separate small JS context (+ up to 48 enlarged relief tiles)
cpu: per request routing; tile enlarging offline

components.name: Compression streams
components.desc: Built-in gzip / deflate (de)compression used for packages, texts and documents.
components.detail: DecompressionStream('gzip') unpacks .gdpkg.gz dictionary packages and .json.gz works in `readPackage` (analysis.js); 'deflate-raw' reads .docx/.odt entries in `zipEntry` (dialogs.js); CompressionStream('deflate-raw') writes zipped exports (export.js). pmtiles.js also uses it for archive directories.

mem: a package is unpacked to one text string (tens of MB for LSJ) before parsing

components.name: Web Workers
components.desc: Background threads for heavy map work, so the page stays responsive.
components.detail: MapLibre runs a worker pool (sized from hardwareConcurrency) for tile parsing; maplibre-contour runs its own worker; both are created from blob URLs. Pult's own scripts run on the main thread.

mem: one JS context per worker (est. 5-20 MB each)
cpu: tile parsing and contours off the main thread

components.name: Canvas 2D
components.desc: 2D drawing for the timeline, map overlays and exports, textures, glyphs and offline relief tiles.
components.detail: getContext('2d') appears in nine scripts (app, library, timeline, map layers, saved maps, sun/sky, relief, TinySDF); OffscreenCanvas and createImageBitmap decode Mapterhorn tiles in the service worker (`enlargeDem`) and in maplibre-contour.

mem: canvases while open (map exports can be large)

components.name: Toolkit entry point
components.desc: `python gd.py <command>`: one command line on the user's Windows PC for every build step of the dictionaries, texts and map packages.
components.detail: Everything (code, raw data, caches, projects, a private Python environment) lives inside the greekdict folder; nothing is installed system-wide. Subcommands dispatch to the modules of the greekdict package.

components.name: Command dispatcher
components.desc: gd.py maps each subcommand (packages, latin, whitaker, texts, annotate, maps, relief, itinere, fetch-maps, scanocr, scanproof, scanclean, lemmas, fetch, build, html) to its module.
components.detail: `reexec` reruns itself inside the private .venv when it exists; project commands check projects/<name>. latin and whitaker also rewrite packages.json afterwards.

components.name: Private Python environment
components.desc: `gd.py setup` creates .venv in the folder and installs lxml and python-docx.
components.detail: The map and relief steps additionally need rasterio, numpy, Pillow, mercantile, pyogrio and shapely (imported on demand with hints), plus the external programs mapshaper and tippecanoe and the npm packages maplibre-gl and pmtiles.

components.name: Windows launchers
components.desc: run_fetch_maps.bat and run_phaedros.bat: double-click starters on the PC.
components.detail: run_fetch_maps.bat runs the long, resumable raw-data download for the maps; run_phaedros.bat runs setup, lemmas, fetch and build for the Phaedros project.

components.name: Tests
components.desc: `gd.py test`: unit tests of normalisation keys, Beta Code and tokenising.
components.detail: tests/test_basic.py runs with unittest.

components.name: Raw data downloads
components.desc: Scripts that download the open source data the builds start from into data/.
components.detail: Downloads are resumable or cached so they run once; only these steps and the CLD fetcher need the internet.

store: data/: GBs (DEM, Natural Earth II, Blue Marble)

components.name: Treebanks, LSJ XML and Eulexis
components.desc: fetch_data.py: UD Ancient Greek treebanks (PROIEL, Perseus), Perseus LSJ XML and the Eulexis Pape/LSJ/analyses files from raw.githubusercontent.com.
components.detail: Afterwards it builds the LSJ entry index (`lsj`) and the form→lemma table (`build_table`). Frisk ships already parsed (data/frisk).

components.name: Map raw data
components.desc: fetchdata.py (gd.py fetch-maps): Copernicus GLO-90 elevation from AWS S3, Natural Earth II and bathymetry from naciscdn.org, Itiner-e roads from Zenodo.
components.detail: Defines the map area `AREA` (-20..80 E, 0..62 N) and the detail `REGIONS` (Greece, Italy, Asia Minor, Levant); reads Copernicus' built-in overviews for the 15" base so only a fraction is downloaded; multi-threaded and resumable.

mem: mosaics of up to tens of thousands of pixels

components.name: Pape and Bailly from the CLD
components.desc: fetch_cld.py: Pape and Bailly entries per lemma from the BBAW Corpus Lexicographicum Digitale JSON API (cld.bbaw.de).
components.detail: Polite by design: one request at a time with a pause (3 s), backoff on HTTP 429, everything cached in data/cache/cld and reused by later projects and by the Bailly package.

components.name: Printed dictionary projects
components.desc: The toolkit's original purpose: a printed (Word) or offline-HTML dictionary for one Greek text, one lemma per page, Frisk – Pape – LSJ – Bailly.
components.detail: A project lives in projects/<name>/ (e.g. phaedros): text.txt in, lemmas.csv, master.json, dictionary.docx and dictionary.html out. Independent of the app; it shares the parsers and caches with the package builds.
components.netNote: the fetch step needs the internet

components.name: Lemmatising
components.desc: lemmatize.py and lemmas.py: text tokens → candidate lemmata from the UD treebank tables, merged with the user's lemma_overrides.csv.
components.detail: Unknown forms are listed for manual entry; the user's overrides always win and survive reruns; lemmas.py checks every lemma is found in the dictionaries.

components.name: Merging the sources
components.desc: merge.py: Frisk, Pape, LSJ and Bailly entries per lemma into master.json.
components.detail: Uses the Frisk index (frisk_index.py over data/frisk), the LSJ adapter (lsj.py, Beta Code via betacode.py) and the CLD cache; accent-insensitive keys from norm.py.

components.name: Word and HTML output
components.desc: build_docx.py (python-docx) and build_html.py: the printable dictionary and a self-contained offline HTML version.
components.detail: Regenerated from master.json at any time (hand edits in the .docx are lost); the HTML sorts by text order or alphabet, folds each lemma and source, and filters accent-insensitively.

components.name: Greek dictionary packages
components.desc: packages.py (gd.py packages): builds the Greek dictionary and morphology packages (*.gdpkg.gz) the app imports, and their manifest.
components.detail: Format 'greekdict-pkg-2': gzip-compressed JSON whose entries are grouped into buckets by accent-free key prefix, so the app stores few large IndexedDB records. Public packages are written to packages/ (copied into the app's packages/); Frisk and Bailly, which may not be published, go to private/ for the private repository.

mem: whole dictionaries in memory while building (hundreds of MB, est.)

components.name: Package writer and buckets
components.desc: `write`, `make_buckets`, `write_dict`: the shared package format used by every dictionary builder.
components.detail: A bucket is an accent-free key prefix of at least 3 letters, lengthened where it holds more than a limit (150 for dictionaries, 400 for morphology); the split list must match `bucketOf` in the app's analysis.js. `add_headwords` adds headword lists for the app's search to existing packages (gd.py packages --headwords).

components.name: Frisk, Pape, LSJ, Bailly
components.desc: One builder per dictionary: `pkg_frisk` (parsed Frisk HTML, with 'mentioned under' links), `pkg_pape` and `pkg_lsj` (Eulexis tab files), `pkg_bailly` (CLD cache or a project's master.json).
components.detail: frisk.py parses the IEED/Leiden HTML once into data/frisk; Eulexis supplies Pape 3.1 and LSJ 6.5.1. Adding a dictionary means one function yielding entries {i, h, k, html}.

store: lsj 14 MB, pape 10 MB, frisk, bailly

components.name: Morphology and hints
components.desc: `pkg_morph`: the Greek form → [lemma, analysis] package (Eulexis/Diogenes analyses, GPL) and the separate morphhints package (preferred lemma per form and word class per lemma from the UD treebanks, CC BY-NC-SA).
components.detail: Handles Beta Code forms with preverbs; the two licences are kept in separate packages.

components.name: Package manifest
components.desc: `manifest`: packages/packages.json with id, file, name, kind, source, licence, size and a 12-character content hash as version.
components.detail: The app compares these versions to offer updates. Called with dest=private/ it copies Frisk and Bailly with their own packages.json for the private repository.

components.name: Latin packages
components.desc: latin.py and whitaker.py: Latin morphology and dictionaries (Collatinus, Lewis & Short, Georges, Whitaker's Words).
components.detail: Lookup keys: lower case, no diacritics, j→i, v→u (`latkey`). Both commands rewrite packages.json afterwards.

mem: all generated forms in memory (est. hundreds of MB)

components.name: Collatinus morphology
components.desc: Generates every form of every lemma from the Collatinus models and lexicon, as Collatinus does, into morph-la and the collatinus dictionary.
components.detail: `load_models`, `generate`, `engine`, `translations` re-implement Collatinus' modele/lemme logic in Python; `pkg_morph_latin` writes form → [lemma, analysis] (GPL-3.0).

components.name: Lewis & Short and Georges
components.desc: `pkg_ls` and `pkg_georges` convert the TEI XML of Lewis & Short (Perseus) and Georges into dictionary packages.
components.detail: `tei_html` turns TEI elements into the app's entry HTML; `tei_entries` keys them by Latin key.

components.name: Whitaker's Words
components.desc: whitaker.py: stem + ending tables as a second Latin analyser (morph-la-ww) and the English meanings as a small dictionary (whitaker).
components.detail: Parses DICTLINE.GEN, INFLECTS.LAT and UNIQUES.LAT; the app analyses a form as stem + ending whose inflection must fit the entry.

components.name: Scanned dictionaries
components.desc: A re-runnable pipeline that turns page scans of copyrighted dictionaries (Walde–Hofmann, Chantraine) into private packages.
components.detail: Separate stages per CONVERSION.md: recognition once, proofreading by page and line, cheap clean-up rules re-run whenever a rule changes, hand corrections applied last so a rebuild never erases them. Output goes only to the private repository.

cpu: ≈15 s per page per core for OCR; ~2,000 pages

components.name: Text recognition
components.desc: scanocr.py: renders PDF pages, trims and splits double pages, and runs Tesseract (deu/lat/grc/fra) into one JSON per page with lines, words, confidence and ink density.
components.detail: The expensive stage, run once per page; nothing is merged or corrected here so line-end hyphens can be judged later.

components.name: Proofreading
components.desc: scanproof.py: prepares page images with numbered lines and review pages (scan beside text, changes marked) for full proofreading.
components.detail: Proofread text is kept per page and line in scans/proof so the clean-up rules still apply; scans/progress.py and sync_pc.py feed a progress dashboard and sync changes to the PC.

components.name: Clean-up and package
components.desc: scanclean.py: rules for hyphens, running heads, abbreviations and Latin vowel lengths, entry splitting, then `write_dict` → walde.gdpkg.gz.
components.detail: Long vowels lost by Tesseract are restored by checking words against German (wordfreq) and all Collatinus forms; hand fixes from scans/fixes/<book>.txt are applied on every run.

components.name: Text packages
components.desc: texts.py, authormeta.py and annotate.py: build the Library's works and catalogue from the open corpora.
components.detail: Licence of all texts: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Perseus, Open Greek and Latin); GLAUx readings CC BY-SA 4.0.

cpu: long batch over thousands of files

components.name: Corpus conversion
components.desc: texts.py (gd.py texts): Perseus canonical-greekLit and -latinLit, First1KGreek and CSEL TEI → one gzip JSON per work (format 'greekdict-work-1').
components.detail: Splits works into books (top-level divisions or groups of small ones) with blocks of paragraphs, verse lines, headings and speakers; gzip with mtime 0 so unchanged texts keep identical files and versions.

components.name: Catalogue and author data
components.desc: catalog.json: authors with date, period and genres (authormeta.py from the TLG canon of CLTK, plus hand additions) and their works with size, word count and version hash.
components.detail: The app's Library, timeline and filters are built from this file.

components.name: Context readings (GLAUx)
components.desc: annotate.py: adds lemma + morphological tag of every word from the GLAUx corpus into the Greek work packages.
components.detail: Uses the app's own tokeniser regex so word counts match; updates each work's size, version and share of annotated words in the catalogue.

components.name: Map packages
components.desc: maps.py (gd.py maps) and itinere.py: build the map packages and the list maps.json.
components.detail: Default output is the app repo's maps/ folder; the published files live in the lesepult-maps repository and maps.json carries that site's address (--url).

components.name: Base map and engines
components.desc: `build_base`: Natural Earth land, lakes, rivers and borders simplified with mapshaper to GeoJSON; `copy_engines`: MapLibre 5.24.0 into base/lib5 and pmtiles.js 4.4.1 into base/lib (MapLibre 4.7 into base/lib).
components.detail: The engines are copied from npm package dist folders (npm pack maplibre-gl@5.24.0 / pmtiles@4.4.1).

components.name: Ancient world layers
components.desc: `build_ancient`: AWMC data → water, empires, provinces, labels, areas, roads, urban, aqueducts, walls, canals (GeoJSON) with period spans.
components.detail: Periods follow the Barrington Atlas codes (A, C, H, R, L → year ranges, `span_of`).

components.name: Pleiades gazetteer
components.desc: `build_places`: the Pleiades places with types, names in original script and romanised, and attested years → places/places.json.
components.detail: `corpus_mentions` checks the names against the texts' works so the app can weight places that the corpus mentions; `TEXT_TYPES` lists the place types searched in a text.

components.name: Vector tile packages
components.desc: `build_landscape_hd` (Landscape – detailed, zoom 4-10, tippecanoe) and itinere.py (Itiner-e Roman roads in two levels of detail) → PMTiles.
components.detail: itinere.py reads the GeoPackage, reprojects and keeps name, main/secondary, certainty, dates, itineraries and builder.

components.name: maps.json and parts
components.desc: `manifest`: the package list with files, size, content hash version, groups and levels, retired flags and the download site; splits files over 16 MB into parts.
components.detail: Whole large files are listed in .gitignore so only their parts are published; relief and Natural Earth II packages are marked retired (replaced by Mapterhorn and Blue Marble).

components.name: Raster tile packages
components.desc: relief.py (gd.py relief): Blue Marble imagery, sea depths and the (now retired) relief and Natural Earth II packages as PMTiles.
components.detail: `build_bluemarble` makes base/bluemarble.pmtiles (WebP, zoom 0-6) from NASA's 21600×10800 April image; `build_bathy` makes relief/bathy.pmtiles from Natural Earth depth zones.

components.name: Elevation tiles (retired)
components.desc: `build`, `terrarium`, `mosaic`, `fill_pits`, `pyramid`: Copernicus GLO-90 → Terrarium WebP tiles in PMTiles, overview and four regions.
components.detail: Replaced in the app by Mapterhorn plus areas saved on the device (v317); the packages remain listed as retired.

components.name: Blue Marble and Natural Earth II
components.desc: `build_bluemarble` (in use) and `build_ne2` (retired) reproject the source images to Web Mercator image tiles.
components.detail: Uses rasterio reprojection, mercantile tile bounds and Pillow WebP encoding.

components.name: Sea depths
components.desc: `build_bathy`: Natural Earth bathymetry shapefiles → one vector layer 'depth' (property d) via mapshaper and tippecanoe.
components.detail: Shallow zones first so deeper ones draw above them.
